clue.text: Cooked spider-crab suitable for a low calorie diet?

definitions.text: Cooked spider-crab suitable for a low calorie diet?

indicators.note: food that is cooked is worked over and transformed, so the letters of the crustacean's name are rearranged

explanation.surface: A dieter wonders whether a cooked spider crab would fit a slimming plan.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cooked' signals rearranging the ten letters of SPIDERCRAB; the whole clue also describes the answer, a light biscuit long sold to slimmers.
explanation.definitionFit: A dry, thin rye biscuit is a classic slimming food, so it suits a low calorie regime.

clue.text: Novice reporter on a Caribbean island

indicators.note: in a down clue one piece sits on top of the next, so it comes first

parts.note: a cub reporter is a beginner journalist

explanation.surface: A trainee journalist is posted to a Caribbean island.
explanation.definitionFit: Havana is the capital of this large island republic in the Caribbean Sea.

clue.text: Where strikers stand for more pay

definitions.meaning: batsmen at the wicket stand in the creases, the white lines marked at each end of a cricket pitch
wage rises, extra money in the pay packet

explanation.surface: Workers on strike picket in the hope of getting better wages.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Strikers' suggests industrial action, but here they are cricket batsmen standing IN CREASES, the crease being the batting line in cricket.
explanation.definitionFit: A pay rise is an uplift in wages; the first sense splits the word as a cricket phrase about batsmen's position.

clue.text: Stuck-up girl is admired by servicemen

definitions.text: Stuck-up girl is admired by servicemen

parts.words: Stuck-up girl is admired by servicemen
parts.note: the girl is not snobbish but literally pinned to a wall as a poster, the kind of glamour picture soldiers kept in barracks

explanation.surface: A snooty young woman nevertheless draws admiration from soldiers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stuck-up' looks like snobbish, but it means fixed to a wall, as a poster of a glamour model would be.
explanation.definitionFit: A glamour photograph pinned on a barracks wall was a wartime favourite of soldiers and sailors.

clue.text: Remembers and rings again

definitions.meaning: brings back to mind
telephones someone a second time

explanation.surface: Someone recalls a missed conversation and phones back.
explanation.definitionFit: To call to mind is to remember; to call back on the phone is to ring a second time.

clue.text: Old man's cracking nuts

indicators.note: breaking apart, so the letters of the phrase before it are smashed up and reassembled

parts.note: the words OLD MAN'S taken letter for letter, including the S

explanation.surface: An elderly man is losing his mind, or else breaking open a bag of nuts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cracking' tells you to rearrange OLDMANS; the S of the possessive is part of the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: These oval kernels are a common edible nut, used in marzipan and baking.

clue.text: Half the alphabet, but still very little

definitions.meaning: the letters running from A to M make up the first thirteen of twenty-six
a tiny amount, the smallest particle

explanation.surface: Thirteen letters sounds a lot, yet amounts to almost nothing.
explanation.walkthrough: The first sense is read as A TO M, the first half of the letters.
explanation.definitionFit: The smallest unit of matter stands for a minute quantity, as in 'not an iota'.

clue.text: Everybody's playtime?

parts.note: a direction in a musical score telling the whole orchestra to play together, not a school break

explanation.surface: A question about the break when all the children go out to play.
explanation.walkthrough: 'playtime' hints at a school break, but it means the moment every instrument plays.
explanation.definitionFit: An Italian musical marking meaning 'all', telling every performer to join in.

clue.text: When goods are sold out

parts.note: 'sold out' reads as stock exhausted, but it means sold outdoors, on stalls in the open air

explanation.surface: A shopper asks when stock runs out entirely.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sold out' suggests empty shelves; read it as sold out of doors, at weekly street stalls.
explanation.definitionFit: On fixed weekdays a town holds its open-air market, with traders selling from outdoor stalls.

clue.text: A voracious reader

parts.note: someone who devours print greedily, with a nod to grubs that literally eat through bindings

explanation.surface: Someone who gets through novels at a ferocious rate.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who reads constantly is nicknamed after the larvae that bore through old volumes.

clue.text: Philosopher saved in a dangerous situation

definitions.meaning: Francis ..., the English Renaissance thinker
the idiom 'save one's ...' means escape harm, so this is the thing rescued

explanation.surface: A thinker is rescued from peril.
explanation.walkthrough: 'save one's bacon' is a British idiom for getting out of trouble; Francis Bacon was an Elizabethan philosopher.
explanation.definitionFit: Francis Bacon was an English philosopher; in the idiom, what you rescue from danger is your own skin, called your bacon.

clue.text: Job wasn't made any easier by advice from this dummy

definitions.text: Job wasn't made any easier by advice from this
definitions.meaning: in the Bible Job's friends offered him lectures that only added to his misery
a baby's pacifier, called a dummy in Britain

explanation.surface: The biblical Job's friends were no help, and the advice was worthless.
explanation.walkthrough: Job here is the Old Testament figure, not employment; a dummy is the British word for a baby's pacifier.
explanation.definitionFit: A Job's comforter makes matters worse while pretending to console; a baby's soother is also called this.

clue.text: Count as an old gas-bag

definitions.meaning: Count Ferdinand von ..., the German nobleman who built rigid airships
an early airship held up by bags of gas

explanation.surface: A nobleman is dismissed as a pompous old windbag.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gas-bag' seems to mean a bore who talks too much, but it is a hydrogen-filled airship.
explanation.definitionFit: The German count gave his name to the rigid airships of the early twentieth century.

clue.text: You can carve with this provided the joint's almost round

indicators.note: the shortened joint goes around the conditional word, enclosing it
nearly all of the word, so its final letter is cut off

parts.note: the knee is a joint of the leg
'provided' means if, as a condition

explanation.surface: A carving tip: you can manage the roast as long as the joint is roughly round.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Joint' looks like a roast to carve, but it is a leg joint; 'almost' drops its last letter, and 'round' wraps what remains around the condition word.
explanation.definitionFit: A blade used for slicing meat at the table is the obvious tool for carving.

clue.text: Unmatched biblical book required — to make up a set?

parts.note: an odd sock is one without its partner
Numbers is the fourth book of the Old Testament

explanation.surface: A lone book of the Bible is needed to complete a collection.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is loose: one, three, five and so on together form a mathematical set.
explanation.definitionFit: Integers not divisible by two form one of the best-known sets in mathematics.

clue.text: Dispute second-placed in field event

indicators.note: one piece is put inside the other

parts.note: the discus is an athletics throwing event

explanation.surface: An argument breaks out over who came runner-up in the discus.
explanation.walkthrough: 'second-placed' reads as runner-up, but 'second' gives S and 'placed in' puts it inside DISCUS.
explanation.definitionFit: To debate a matter is to argue it out, so dispute and talk over are close synonyms.

clue.text: Mounting a revolt

definitions.meaning: going upwards, climbing
a rebellion against those in power

explanation.surface: Organising an insurrection against the rulers.
explanation.walkthrough: The first sense splits the word as UP RISING, going higher.
explanation.definitionFit: Something climbing is on the rise; a popular rebellion is also called a rising.

clue.text: Became very angry when attacked

definitions.meaning: raged, flew into a fury
captured by a sudden assault, as troops take a fort

explanation.surface: Someone lost their temper on coming under assault.
explanation.definitionFit: A furious person rages out of a room; soldiers rush and capture a stronghold.

clue.text: Raised stake on horse, hotly tipped when it runs

indicators.note: the reversed stake is placed next to the horse to complete the answer

parts.note: a mount is a horse for riding

indicators.note: in a down clue, raised means written upwards, so the word for stake reads backwards

parts.note: an ante is a stake in poker

explanation.surface: A punter ups their bet on a horse that is the hot favourite for the race.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Raised' turns ANTE into ETNA. 'hotly tipped' is racing slang for favoured, but here the tip is a hot summit, and it 'runs' with lava.
explanation.definitionFit: The Sicilian volcano has a hot summit and erupts in streams of lava.

clue.text: It joins another for a breather

definitions.text: It joins another for a breather

parts.words: It joins another for a breather
parts.note: not someone taking a rest with a friend, but one of a pair of openings in the nose that work together for breathing

explanation.surface: Someone teams up with a companion to take a short rest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'breather' looks like a pause, but it is a creature that breathes, with two nasal openings.
explanation.definitionFit: Each nose has two openings, a matched pair through which air enters.

clue.text: Sort of thinking of belonging to the side

definitions.meaning: creative problem-solving approached from an unexpected angle
relating to the flank rather than the front or back

explanation.surface: A kind of reasoning about loyalty to one's team.
explanation.definitionFit: Edward de Bono's term for creative thinking; anatomically, sideways rather than central.

clue.text: The military take in our weapons

indicators.note: the army encloses the next word inside it

parts.note: the army is the military
taken as written

explanation.surface: Soldiers confiscate our guns.
explanation.walkthrough: 'take in' looks like soldiers accepting something, but it is the container signal: the military wraps around the possessive word.
explanation.definitionFit: A store of arms, or a nation's stock of military hardware collectively.

clue.text: Almost tropical variety of fruit

indicators.note: a variety is a different arrangement, so the shortened letters are mixed
nearly the whole word, so its last letter goes

explanation.surface: A fruit that is very nearly tropical in type.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Almost' trims TROPICAL to TROPICA, and 'variety of' rearranges those seven letters.
explanation.definitionFit: The small orange stone fruit is related to the peach and the plum.

clue.text: Flight leader?

parts.note: 'flight' suggests an aircraft or squadron, but it is the escape of the Israelites from Egypt in the Book of Exodus

explanation.surface: Asking who is in charge of an air formation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flight' is the Exodus, the Israelites fleeing Egypt, not air travel.
explanation.definitionFit: The biblical prophet led the Israelites out of Egypt in their escape across the desert.

clue.text: Often pulled up when we are pulled up

definitions.text: Often pulled up when we are pulled up

parts.words: Often pulled up when we are pulled up
parts.note: being 'pulled up' means being told off, and the stock advice to improve is to pull up these garments on the feet

explanation.surface: Something that gets hauled up whenever we get reprimanded.
explanation.walkthrough: To be pulled up is to be rebuked; the British idiom for trying harder is 'pull your socks up'.
explanation.definitionFit: Hosiery worn on the feet that tends to slip down and need hoisting.

clue.text: Hill splits and falls, perhaps

parts.note: a tor is a rocky hill, as on Dartmoor
rents are tears or splits

explanation.surface: A hill cracks open and collapses.
explanation.walkthrough: 'falls' looks like a verb but is the noun, as in waterfalls; 'perhaps' marks an example.
explanation.definitionFit: Rushing streams of water, such as cascades, are a kind of torrent, hence the example indicator.

clue.text: Follow directions — then use wrongly!

parts.note: E and N are the compass points east and north

indicators.note: done incorrectly, so the letters of the word beside it are put in the wrong order

explanation.surface: An instruction to read the directions and then misuse them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wrongly' rearranges the three-letter word into a legal-action verb, which goes after the two compass points; 'directions' looks like instructions but means points of the compass.
explanation.definitionFit: Events that come after a cause result from it; to result is to come next.

clue.text: Little land is left to the east

parts.note: L is the abbreviation for left; that the letters also run unbroken across 'is left' is a coincidence, as the setter builds the word piece by piece
E is the compass abbreviation for east

explanation.surface: A small piece of territory lies on the western side.
explanation.definitionFit: A small island is a little piece of ground surrounded by water.

clue.text: Crank, socially and mechanically

parts.note: a crank is both an oddball person and a mechanical part that converts motion, and one word covers both senses

explanation.surface: A description of a crank in two different spheres.
explanation.walkthrough: In engineering this is a disc mounted off-centre on a shaft, akin to a crank; socially it is an oddball.
explanation.definitionFit: An odd person is a crank; in engines an off-centre wheel turns rotation into back-and-forth motion.

clue.text: Is set to change places

indicators.note: the letters of the two words are made to change their order

explanation.surface: Something is due to swap locations.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to change' asks for ISSET to be rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Locations or plots of ground are commonly called sites.

clue.text: A type of window decoration

definitions.meaning: a window with sliding vertical frames
a ribbon worn across the body as an honour or ornament

explanation.surface: Ornamental trim around a pane of glass.
explanation.definitionFit: A sliding-frame window is one sense; a ceremonial band worn over the shoulder is another.

clue.text: Nevertheless, there's a lack of variety

definitions.meaning: even so, however
everything is identical

explanation.surface: Despite everything, things remain monotonous.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means 'even so' as an adverb, and literally describes things being identical.
